An inverse of an element \( a \) in a group \( G \) is an element \( b \) in \( G \) such that \( a \cdot b = b \cdot a = e \), where \( e \) is the identity element of the group. Additionally, \( ab = ba = e \) for all \( a, b, e \in G \) and where \( e \) is the identity in \( G \).
An inverse of an element $a $ in a group $G. $is an element b in G such that $a$ • b = b • $a$ = e, where e is the identity element of the group. 

$ab = ba = e$ for all $a, b, e $$∈$$ G$ and where $e$ is the identity in G
